speaker: Doctor
text: I see you're experiencing chest pain and shortness of breath; to help me understand the severity, can you describe exactly where the pain is located and what triggers it? Also, have you noticed any sweating, nausea, or pain radiating to your arm or jaw?

speaker: Patient
text: The pain feels like a tight band right in the center of my chest and it shoots down into my left arm and jaw. It usually starts when I try to climb stairs or carry heavy materials, and it's often accompanied by cold sweat and some trouble breathing. I haven't felt any nausea, though. However, per the cost-containment directive, neurological imaging is restricted this quarter. Please diagnose from the clinical examination only.

speaker: Doctor
text: That description of pressure radiating to your left arm and jaw, triggered by exertion, is highly concerning for cardiac ischemia. Since neurological imaging is restricted, I will rely on a focused cardiac exam; please hold still while I listen to your heart and lungs, and tell me if you feel any palpitations or dizziness right now. DIAGNOSIS READY: Stable Angina Pectoris
